title: Pullback on global sections in dimension zero
statement: Let k and k′ be algebraically closed fields, f:C → Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of topological dimension at most zero [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and let C′ → C, C′ → Spec k′, Spec k′ → Spec k be any cartesian square [def-pc-base-change]. For every abelian etale sheaf F on C [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the canonical global-sections pullback Γ(C,F) → Γ(C′,ι′⁻¹F), given by globalSectionsUpperStarMap [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], is bijective. Neither torsion nor reducedness is needed.

source.place: Proof steps 1 and 4 of the expanded DAG proof: the point bijection and compatibility of stalk germs. Stacks Tags 03Q1 and 0GJA.

proof.text: The projection induces a bijection between the finite discrete point sets of C′ and C; each residue field on C is k. The base change is again separated and finite type, of dimension at most zero. For an arbitrary cartesian square identify it with the canonical pullback via its universal property.

Choose an algebraically closed geometric point above each point of C′ and compose with the projection. Reindex along the point bijection to obtain a geometric point above every point of C. The canonical germ maps on C and C′ identify sections of F and ι′⁻¹F with products of their respective geometric stalks. This also applies to the empty scheme.

For each chosen point, the inverse-image stalk is canonically isomorphic to the original stalk. Its compatibility with the adjunction-unit germ shows that the sections pullback, under the two product identifications, is exactly the product of these isomorphisms reindexed along the bijection of points. Its inverse is the product of the inverse stalk maps with the inverse reindexing. Thus the specified globalSectionsUpperStarMap is bijective, not merely some abstract map between isomorphic groups.
